summary: Reproduced the reported missing ReplaySSM cursor reset at the extra_buffer ping-pong ownership boundaries, reset recycled cursors on initial allocation and replacement installation, and permit extra_buffer only for GDN while retaining the KDA safety guard.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: initial recycled cursors remained [5, 7] and the donation replacement cursor remained 9; 2 failed, 1 passed.
Passing-after regression and boundaries: allocation reset, donation replacement reset, non-ReplaySSM behavior, GDN extra_buffer admission, and KDA extra_buffer rejection; 5 passed.
On AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950, actual device-tensor advanced indexing changed recycled slot 5's ReplaySSM cursor from 9 to 0 and synchronized successfully.
17 nearby tests passed; one unrelated CUDA-only CuTeDSL import test was blocked on this ROCm host by missing cuda.bindings.
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, AST, CI registry, and policy hooks passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: gpu-cursor-check.txt records AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, and write_pos [0, 0, 0, 5, 7, 0] after resetting recycled slot 5.

remaining_limitations: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B weights and an NVIDIA H200 are unavailable, so the reported end-to-end cached_tokens and TTFT measurements were not repeated.
The gfx950 fixture validates the corrected device-tensor ownership/reset operation, not Qwen3.8 semantic accuracy or H200 performance.
KDA extra_buffer remains intentionally unsupported because KDA does not force-flush pending ReplaySSM ring entries at radix tracking boundaries.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
One nearby CUDA-only test could not import cuda.bindings in the prepared ROCm environment.
